environment.note: Windows host, 14 cores. playwright.config.js sizes workers as ceil(cores/4) capped at 4, so this host runs 4 workers and a 2-core CI runner runs 1.

change.mechanism: test.slow() on tests/collision.spec.js 'no buried start position'
change.verifiedBy: a throwaway spec printing test.info().timeout with and without test.slow()
change.rejectedAlternative: raising `timeout` in playwright.config.js, which would mask the #130 class across every spec

runs.note: One test failed; its log was not captured. It was NOT this test, which passed at 38.3 s. Six later captured runs were clean. Most likely the game.spec.js flake seen on unmodified main during #161.

caveat: The post-change durations are tighter than the pre-change ones partly because #161 removed 2.3 MB of source maps from dist/, reducing static-server contention. The exposure is the local 4-worker full-suite run, not CI.

ciRun.finding: CI is FASTER than the 14-core host, not slower: with one worker the sweep runs without contention. Every observed timeout came from a 4-worker local full-suite run. An earlier note in this evidence claimed a 2-core runner would have less headroom; that was backwards and is corrected here and in the test comment.
